title: Iki plugin (iki/v1)
description: A plugin's `plugin.yaml`: its name, what it depends on, and the settings it takes.

name.description: The plugin's name, as `namespace/name`: your lab's or company's namespace, such as `acme/assays`. Its types are `acme/assays.Type`, and its tables start with `acme__assays_`. The `iki` namespace is Iki's own.

version.description: The plugin's release, as a semantic version such as `1.4.0`. Deployments pin the git commit; this is for people.

license.description: The plugin's license, as an SPDX expression such as `Apache-2.0` or `LicenseRef-Acme-Internal`.

homepage.description: Where to read about the plugin (https only).

iki.description: The Iki releases the plugin works with, as comparisons with release numbers separated by commas, such as `>=0.1,<0.3`. A deployment on any other release refuses it. Leaving it out says nothing either way.

dependencies.description: Other plugins this one uses, by name (such as `iki/protein`), with the schema versions of their types it works with.

roles.description: The lab roles this plugin declares, such as `analyst`, `reviewer` and `qa`, by name (ADR 0116). A project's Admins give them to its members, people or teams, beside their project role, and a type's transitions and a workflow step's approval can require one. Elsewhere a role is `namespace/plugin.role`, such as `acme/assays.qa`.

label.description: What people see, such as `QA` or `Reviewer`.

description.description: What someone with the role does, shown where Admins give it, such as `Releases reviewed samples`.

versionConstraint.description: Comparisons with whole schema versions, separated by commas, such as `>=2` or `>=2,<4`.
